title: Lesson 57 - Right-Sizing Data Mappers and IPs Inside OmniScripts: The Architecture View
description: Provide guidance on the appropriate Data Mappers and Integration Procedures to use within an Omniscript to efficiently fetch, transform, and save data to meet specific business outcomes.

questions.question: An OmniScript needs to load a single account record by ID and display a few fields. What is the best fit?
options: An Integration Procedure that calls an external system
A Data Raptor that loads the account by ID
A FlexCard that queries the account
A scheduled Apex job that caches the account
questions.explanation: A Data Raptor is the direct, light way to load a single record by ID into the OmniScript's JSON. An Integration Procedure adds a server round trip for a simple local read. A FlexCard is a display component, not a data source for an OmniScript. A scheduled job is for background work, not an on-demand load.

questions.question: The same multi-source aggregation is needed by three OmniScripts and a FlexCard. Where should the logic live?
options: In a single shared Integration Procedure
In a Data Raptor inside one script
In a custom setting that stores the result
questions.explanation: A single shared Integration Procedure centralizes the aggregation so all consumers reuse one tested artifact. Duplicating it in each script creates drift. A Data Raptor inside one script is not shared. A custom setting stores configuration, not a live aggregation result.

questions.question: An OmniScript must save a parent record and several child records that must all succeed together. What is the best approach?
options: A save Data Raptor that writes the parent only
An Integration Procedure that orchestrates the multi-record save with error handling
A separate Data Raptor for each record with no coordination
A FlexCard that submits the records
questions.explanation: An Integration Procedure can orchestrate the multi-record save and handle errors so a partial write does not leave the data inconsistent. A Data Raptor writing only the parent loses the children. Separate uncoordinated Data Raptors risk partial writes. A FlexCard is a display component and does not orchestrate saves.
